ai.literal: With milk, honey having mixed, it is like that indeed: of the gentle-worded one, from the white teeth seeped liquid.
ai.translation: The liquid seeping from the white teeth of this gentle-worded woman is as sweet as honey mixed with milk.
ai.modern: மென்மையான சொற்களைப் பேசும் இவளுடைய வெண்மையான பற்களில் ஊறிய நீர், பாலோடு தேன் கலந்தாற் போன்ற இனிமை உடையது.
ai.explanation: The couplet describes the sweetness of the lover's kiss through the voice of the hero. He compares the liquid (நீர்) that springs (ஊறிய) from the pure white teeth (வால் எயிறு) of his lover to a delicious mixture of milk and honey (பாலொடு தேன் கலந்து அற்றே). The compound 'பணிமொழி' (gentle words) functions as a metonymy for the woman herself, highlighting her soft and endearing speech. The comparison to milk and honey emphasizes both the purity and the intense, natural sweetness of her affection.

ai.literal: With the body, life's connection is what, indeed like that is with the woman our connection's bond.
ai.translation: Whatever the bond is between the physical body and life, such is the bond between this young woman and me.
ai.modern: உடம்புக்கும் உயிருக்கும் இடையே உள்ள உறவு எத்தன்மையதோ, அத்தன்மையதே இந்த இளம்பெண்ணுக்கும் எனக்கும் இடையே உள்ள காதல் உறவாகும்.
ai.explanation: The speaker compares his love for the young woman to the inseparable connection between a physical body and the life force that animates it. Just as a body cannot function without life, and life in this world requires a body, the lovers are completely dependent on each other. The word 'naṭpu', which usually means friendship, is used here to denote the deep, intimate bond of romantic love.

ai.literal: In the dark pupil / O image! you / go away, we / love / to the beautiful forehead / is not / space.
ai.translation: O image in the dark pupil of my eye, please leave! There is no room for my beloved with the beautiful forehead whom I love.
ai.modern: என் கண்ணின் கருமணியில் உள்ள பாவாய், நீ வெளியே போ! நான் விரும்பும் அழகிய நெற்றியை உடைய என் காதலி அங்கே இருக்க இடம் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker playfully addresses the tiny reflection, or 'image', naturally seen in the dark pupil of the eye. He asks this image to step aside and leave to make space for his beloved. By claiming there is no room for both the reflection and the woman he loves, he poetically expresses the depth of his affection. His beloved occupies his entire vision and mind, leaving no space for anything else.

ai.literal: Living to the soul she is like, the woman with choice jewels; dying to that she is like, at the time of departing.
ai.translation: This woman wearing choice jewels is like life itself to my soul. When she leaves me, she is like death to it.
ai.modern: இந்த அழகிய அணிகலன்களை அணிந்தவள் என்னோடு இருக்கும்போது என் உயிருக்கு வாழ்வு போன்றவள். என்னை விட்டுப் பிரியும்போதோ அந்த உயிருக்குச் சாவு போன்றவள்.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses how completely his existence depends on his lover. He compares her presence to the very act of living for his soul. Conversely, any separation from her, even for a short time, feels exactly like death to his soul. The contrast between living and dying highlights the intensity of his love.

ai.literal: I will think indeed I if forget; forgetting I know not, bright battling eyed woman's qualities.
ai.translation: I would only need to think of her if I ever forgot her. But I never forget the qualities of the woman with bright, battling eyes.
ai.modern: நான் அவளை மறந்தால்தானே நினைப்பதற்கு? ஒளியுடைய போர் செய்யும் கண்களை உடையவளின் குணங்களை நான் ஒருபோதும் மறப்பதே இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses the constancy of his love by playing with the concepts of remembering and forgetting. He states that one only needs to actively remember someone if they have been forgotten. Since the sweet qualities of his lover never leave his mind, he never experiences forgetting her, and thus never has to make an effort to remember her. The phrase 'battling eyes' is a classical poetic image capturing the captivating, piercing nature of her gaze that has conquered his heart.

ai.literal: Eye from-inside he-will-not-go; if-blinked will-he-suffer? Subtle-one my lover.
ai.translation: My lover will not depart from within my eyes; if I blink, will he suffer? So subtle is he.
ai.modern: என் காதலர் என் கண்ணுக்குள்ளிருந்து வெளியேற மாட்டார். நான் கண்ணிமைத்தால் அவர் துன்பப்படுவாரா? அந்த அளவுக்கு அவர் நுட்பமானவர்.
ai.explanation: The speaker marvels at how her lover constantly occupies her vision. She imagines him living inside her eyes, refusing to leave. Because he is so subtle and tiny to fit there, she fears that even the simple act of blinking might cause him to suffer. The word 'பருகுவரா' (will he consume pain or suffer) highlights her delicate care for his subtle form.

words.gloss: he who is inside the eyes

parts.gloss: I do not (1st person plural negative)

ai.literal: He who is inside the eyes - lover - since he is - eyes even - I do not paint - hiding - knowing.
ai.translation: Since my lover dwells inside my eyes, I do not even paint them with kohl, knowing it would hide him.
ai.modern: என் காதலர் என் கண்ணுக்குள்ளேயே இருப்பதால், மை தீட்டினால் அவர் மறைந்துவிடுவார் என்று அறிந்து நான் என் கண்களுக்கு மை தீட்டவும் மாட்டேன்.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses her deep, constant awareness of her lover's presence by imagining that he literally resides inside her eyes. Because of this, she refuses to apply kohl (eye makeup), fearing that the dark paste would cover and hide him. The word 'எழுதேம்' refers to the traditional practice of painting the eyes, and 'கரப்பாக்கு' indicates the act of concealing. This poetic exaggeration highlights the intensity of her love and her desire to keep him always in her sight.

words.gloss: he who is in the heart

ai.literal: As the lover is he who is in the heart, eating hot things we fear, knowing the burning.
ai.translation: Since my lover resides in my heart, I fear eating hot food, knowing it would burn him.
ai.modern: என் காதலர் என் நெஞ்சத்திற்குள் இருப்பதால், அவருக்குச் சுடும் என்பதை அறிந்து நான் சூடான உணவை உண்ணப் பயப்படுகிறேன்.
ai.explanation: The heroine expresses the depth of her love by imagining her lover physically residing within her heart. Because he is always there, she avoids eating hot food. She fears that the heat of the food will burn him. This delicate hyperbole illustrates how constantly she holds him in her thoughts and how deeply she cares for his well-being.

ai.literal: If blink, that he will hide I know; for just that, stranger says this town.
ai.translation: I know that if I blink, he will be hidden from my sight. For just that reason, this town calls him a stranger who lacks love.
ai.modern: நான் கண்களை இமைத்தால் அவர் மறைந்துவிடுவார் என்று எனக்குத் தெரியும். அதனால் நான் இமைக்காமல் இருக்கிறேன்; அதற்காகவே இந்த ஊர் மக்கள் அவரை அன்பில்லாதவர் என்று பழித்துச் சொல்கிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The heroine explains why she never closes her eyes. She knows that if she blinks, her lover, who resides in her eyes, will be hidden from her sight. Because she keeps her eyes open constantly, they show signs of distress, leading the townspeople to mistakenly think he has abandoned her. The word 'ஏதிலர்' literally means strangers, but here it takes the specific sense of unloving or cruel people. Thus, the town wrongly calls him unloving, simply because she refuses to blink.

ai.literal: rejoicing he dwells inside the heart always; separating he dwells, stranger, says this town.
ai.translation: He dwells joyfully in my heart forever. Yet this town says he dwells apart and is a stranger.
ai.modern: அவர் என் உள்ளத்தில் எப்போதும் மகிழ்ந்து வாழ்கிறார். ஆனால் இந்த ஊர் மக்கள் அவர் என்னைப் பிரிந்து வாழும் அன்பில்லாதவர் என்று கூறுகிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks about her lover's constant presence in her mind despite his physical absence. She says that he always dwells joyfully within her heart. However, the ignorant townspeople, seeing only his physical absence, claim that he has separated from her and become an unloving stranger. The contrast between her inner reality and the town's perception highlights the depth of her love.
